best_for: Windows admins and support techs who need to find which process has a file locked, or which DLL version a program loaded, without installing anything.
description:
Process Explorer is part of Sysinternals, Microsoft's collection of utilities for looking inside Windows. Its author also co-wrote the Windows Internals book and the official guide to the Sysinternals tools.

The download comes with a help file that walks through how it works. Sysinternals also makes command-line cousins for scripts: Handle lists open handles, ListDLLs lists loaded DLLs, and PsList and PsKill list and end processes on local or remote PCs. Questions go to the Process Explorer section on Microsoft Q&A.

points.title: Find who has a file open
points.text: A search shows which processes hold a given handle or have a given DLL loaded. That answers the classic question of what is locking a file or folder.

points.title: Two panes, two views
points.text: The top pane lists running processes and the accounts that own them. The bottom pane shows either the selected process's open handles or its loaded DLLs and memory-mapped files.

points.title: Useful for leaks and DLL mix-ups
points.text: Microsoft pitches it for tracking down handle leaks and DLL version problems, and for seeing how Windows and apps behave under the hood.

points.title: No installer at all
points.text: It is a single `procexp.exe` in a zip, about 3.7 MB, with builds for x86, x64 and Arm64. You can also run it straight from Sysinternals Live without downloading.

points.title: Windows 11 and Server 2019 or later
points.text: The current release lists Windows 11 on the client side and Windows Server 2019 and newer. Windows 10 is not on the list, so older PCs may need an older copy from elsewhere.

points.title: Free, but not open source
points.text: Process Explorer is a free Microsoft Sysinternals tool under Microsoft's license terms, written by Mark Russinovich. This listing keeps only the current version.
